title: Pay through a pool without paying twice

blocks.text: A chain of stores pays through a `MUXPool` over two links to its acquirer. Since the second link was added, two complaints have come in. On Tuesday a link dropped at noon, and a few cardholders were charged twice for one purchase, although the checkout showed a single approval. And during the nightly maintenance, when both links are down, every checkout hangs for a second before failing, and the reversal queue fills with purchases the acquirer has never seen.
`Checkout.pay` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/Checkout.java` already handles purchases the host answers. Finish the two methods marked `TODO`:

items: `onNoAnswer(...)`: what a purchase with no answer becomes.

blocks.text: Purchases that must be reversed go onto the `TO_REVERSE` queue of the space (`sp.out`), where the reversal sender takes them. About four lines in total.
The tests run a real round-robin `MUXPool` over two real QMUXes, with a test host behind each link.

cases.says: a purchase the host answers is approved or declined by field 39 and leaves nothing to reverse
a purchase with no answer is an unknown outcome and is never handed to the pool again, where another link would take it
a purchase with no answer may have been approved, so it is queued for reversal
with no usable link the purchase is reported unavailable before anything is sent, and nothing is queued for reversal

origin.section: 14.5 With Nothing Usable, the Pool Spends the Request's Own Time

concepts: A pool chooses a member once per request and never moves it, so a null from the pool is an unknown outcome to reverse; a retry through the pool lands on another link as a second purchase.
With nothing usable the pool polls once a second inside the request's own budget and returns null with nothing sent, so the caller checks isConnected first.
